newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high, seen extending gains.

text.p: Polish shares set a 34-month high in higher turnover on Thursday and analysts expected a new record on Friday though they were not sure about the market's later trend.
The main market's WIG index rose two percent, to 16,914.2, and turnover rose 14.3 percent to 206.6 million zlotys ($68.9 million) on both markets as 72 issues rose, six fell and nine were flat.

Analysts said strong buying after price fixing and rises in continuous trade after the regular session signalled that demand was strong enough to push the WIG index to a new high on Friday, above the psychological resistance of 17,000 points.

"There was strong post-price-fixing buying so we should have more growth tomorrow, but then supply and demand will fight at order balancing," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.

Some analysts said the bourse, though fairly priced with an average price-earnings ratio of about 16, still had upside potential as Poland's economic prospects were good and firms' earnings this year were expected to grow at a fast pace.
They said the current growth might be being spurred by the recent release of companies' earnings for the fourth quarter and all of 1996, as certain firms had revised up earlier 1996 reports.
But some chartists said a double-peak formation might soon appear on the WIG, which could suggest falls to about 15,000.
They said top gainers construction firms Elektrobudowa and Mostostal Krakow, which rose 7.4 and six percent respectively, were helped by an expected increase in construction in Poland.
In 16.7-million-zloty ($5.6 million) continuous trade the WIG 20 index rose 2.2 percent to 1,779.8.
